observations: The earliest authoritative current-layer failure is real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface. Its blockers are verification-contract failures: the simulation source identity does not bind the current identity document, compile authority and ordered-command authority references do not bind exact Vivado export facts, and simulator executables are not authorized by the current tool profile or cited export. No RTL causal module has been identified.

functional_sim is a failed dependency aggregate rather than executed board functional evidence. The VCS functional simulation, VCS analyzer, and AXI/deadlock diagnostic tools were not run because case_axi_ddr_interface failed.

The pending VCS analyzer entry contains an Illegal timescale diagnostic, but its execution status is not_run and the associated diagnosis is historical_only because a live source hash changed and the diagnosis binding is invalid. It must not drive an RTL repair; a fresh analyzer run is required after the current manifest is repaired.

The board semantic evidence report verification/semantic_evidence/board_axi_ddr.json is missing. Therefore there is no current board value, numeric, data-order, AXI, DDR, liveness, complete-weight-consumption, lifecycle-frontier, or output evidence, even though lower scopes have semantic certificates.

The current hierarchy records operator-leaf and single-transformer-layer gates as pass, and hierarchical_learning_context is hash-validated with no lower-layer challenge. The connected-kernel timing invariant is an elastic variable-latency token pipeline with preserved boundary order and required cross-token overlap; unequal same-cycle start or finish is not a failure. These lower-layer facts remain reusable and must not be replayed without a direct current contradiction.

The current hierarchical table records case_board_interface_discovery as pass, but exact wrapper/source identity and authority binding still require current validation as part of the manifest repair. Historical interface-failure records in SACG are rejected artifacts and cannot be used as a current diagnosis or as permission to guess a replacement source.

sacg_memory_truth is authoritative for this scope: it reports 16 active contamination barriers and 6 open retry requests, with zero open backtrack requests for the named scope. Rejected Stage7 and Stage8 artifacts remain planning/debug evidence only. The refined current-stage contract may supersede same-stage retry artifacts only after its own checks pass; until then, the retry requests remain downstream-consumption blockers.

The conditional design-team router returned no_split because the failure class is deterministic and unambiguous. No specialist review was triggered, and its absence cannot replace current checker or real-tool evidence.
proposed_actions: Create a new hash-bound current-stage repair candidate that rebinds the exact sample-project wrapper and source set, exact Vivado export facts, compile authority, ordered-command authority references, and simulator authorization without changing design or verification inputs.
Rerun case_axi_ddr_interface and the required artifact/tool-protocol checks; keep all dependent simulation gates blocked if identity or authority binding still fails.

After the interface gate passes, execute the real board-wrapped VCS simulation with fresh boundary monitors, VCS analysis, and AXI/deadlock observation; use targeted replay only on a current localized failure slice.

If a real current trace identifies a board-wrapper, loader, scheduler, memory, order, protocol, or lifecycle fault, repair only that localized current-layer slice and rerun the same layer. Reopen a lower layer only for the explicitly required direct hash-bound contradiction.

Once current-layer execution is valid, run the remaining multilayer functional, deadlock, AXI protocol, DDR roundtrip, semantic-evidence, weight-consumption, numeric, order, and frontier checks, then return a new Stage7 result. Do not promote before all required gates pass.
risks: An unbound identity or unauthorized compile command could simulate different sources or a different board contract while appearing to execute successfully.

Until a fresh VCS run completes, the system has no evidence for output values, numeric tolerance compliance, token/data order, AXI protocol behavior, DDR image roundtrip, liveness, weight consumption, or output/lifecycle frontier progress.
Repairing the stale Illegal timescale diagnosis or any downstream symptom without current hash-bound evidence could introduce an unrelated RTL change and violate the hierarchical repair loop.

A manifest or weight file on disk is insufficient: the board harness must bind the complete in-scope tensor catalog and produce executed loader/consumption evidence for every required Transformer-block tensor.

Board-level integration can diverge from model, shape, numeric policy, memory layout, runtime ABI, transfer counts, address map, and data-order contracts even when leaf and single-layer certificates remain valid.
Independent AXI or prefetch activity could be mistaken for output-frontier progress; no board liveness or output pass may be inferred from such activity.
Active SACG contamination barriers and repeated retry records create a retry-spin risk; old repair plans and verification results must not be consumed as validated inputs or silently promoted.
Adding embedding, tokenization, final norm, logits, sampling, or other tail work to the DUT or golden would invalidate the functional scope and weight-coverage contract.

Keep checkpoint, deterministic or real input provenance, target-model reference outputs, numeric comparison policy and tolerance, semantic testbench contract, and source hashes immutable during repair.

Require a complete target-checkpoint tensor catalog, same-input target-model inference, generated semantic testbench hashes, and executed proof that every required Transformer-block weight was consumed by the DUT loader/harness.
Transformer blocks are the complete DUT scope; exclude embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, sampling, and other model-tail work from DUT weights and golden boundaries.
Do not treat a present or ready-looking trace file, manifest, weight file, or rejected Stage7/Stage8 artifact as executed validation evidence.
A board output-frontier stall is localization evidence only; distinguish independent AXI/prefetch progress from output and lifecycle-frontier progress.
Do not reopen passed lower layers without a current hash-bound trace naming direct core start, ingress, egress, causal boundary, and contradiction of the current lower-layer certificate.
No backend synthesis, implementation, bitstream, runtime-ABI, or board-runtime promotion until all required current-layer gates pass.
